title: Extraction and Quantification of Water Buffalo Milk Proteins via RP-HPLC-DAD and NIRS
author: Julián Andrés Castillo Vargas
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.pex-1423/v1
materials: - Solutions and material preparation: 30 min - The extraction of protein variants: a batch of 24 samples: 101 min. - The total time of the chromatographic analysis (per sample): 53 min (13 min of equilibrium + 40 min of chromatographic run). - NIRS analysis: 5 min.
See figures section for more details.

steps.title: Thaw frozen milk samples
steps.instruction: On the day of analysis, thaw any frozen milk samples at room temperature (25 °C) until completely liquid.

steps.title: Homogenize sample if particulates present
steps.instruction: If the milk contains solid particulate material (e.g., after long storage or freeze‑thaw), shake the container vigorously to obtain a homogeneous aliquot; discard the sample if a representative suspension cannot be achieved.

steps.title: Aliquot milk into Eppendorf tube
steps.instruction: Pipette 1 mL of milk into a 2.2 mL Eppendorf tube using an automatic pipette.

steps.title: Add solution A (1:1 ratio)
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of solution A to the tube, giving a sample : solution A ratio of 1 : 1.

steps.title: Vortex mixture briefly
steps.instruction: Shake each mixture in a vortex for 10 seconds at medium speed.

steps.title: Incubate at room temperature
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture at 25 °C for 1 hour; the room can be climate‑controlled with an air‑conditioning unit to maintain the temperature.

steps.title: Centrifuge mixture
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 14 200 × g for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Remove upper fat layer
steps.instruction: Using a micro‑spatula, carefully remove the upper fat layer formed after centrifugation.

steps.title: Dilute supernatant with solution B
steps.instruction: Transfer 450 µL of the supernatant to a new 2.2 mL Eppendorf tube and add 1 350 µL of solution B (supernatant : solution B = 1 : 3).

steps.title: Prepare HPLC injection vial
steps.instruction: Transfer 1 mL of the mixture to an HPLC vial and store the vial at 4 °C until analysis.

steps.title: Configure RP-HPLC-DAD parameters
steps.instruction: Set the RP‑HPLC‑DAD system to: column temperature 45 °C; injection volume 5 µL; stationary phase Hypersil GOLD C8 (3 µm, 150 × 4.6 mm) with a Hypersil GOLD C8 guard column (5 µm, 10 mm); detection wavelength 214 nm; gradient mode with a constant flow of 0.500 mL/min according to the elution gradient in Table 1; run an equilibrium program before each sample and verify the column’s flow‑rate limits.

steps.title: Inject sample and acquire chromatogram
steps.instruction: Inject the refrigerated sample (manually or via autosampler) and record the chromatogram.

steps.title: Determine total protein by NIRS
steps.instruction: Using a NIRS instrument, determine the total protein and casein contents in g/100 g milk and also measure the milk density.

steps.title: Integrate peak areas for proteins
steps.instruction: From the chromatogram, integrate the peak area of each protein: casein variants κ‑CN X2, α s2‑CN, κ‑CN X1, α s1‑CN B, α s1‑CN A, βγ‑CN and whey proteins α‑La and β‑Lg. Note that some casein variants may be absent in a given sample.

steps.title: Calculate casein variant concentrations
steps.instruction: Compute casein variant concentrations using the following steps:

substeps.instruction: Calculate total casein area = sum of all casein variant peak areas.
For each variant, calculate proportion = (variant peak area) / (total casein area).
Concentration of variant (g/100 g milk) = casein content (g/100 g milk) × proportion.
Optional: Convert to g/L using milk density (g/mL) × 10.

steps.title: Calculate whey protein variant concentrations
steps.instruction: Compute whey protein variant concentrations using the following steps:

substeps.instruction: Calculate total whey area = sum of whey protein peak areas.
For each whey variant, calculate proportion = (variant peak area) / (total whey area).
Whey protein content (g/100 g milk) = total milk protein (g/100 g milk) – casein content (g/100 g milk).
Concentration of variant (g/100 g milk) = whey protein content × proportion.
Optional: Convert to g/L using milk density (g/mL) × 10.

steps.title: Record results and perform calculations
steps.instruction: Enter all peak‑area data, calculated proportions, and concentrations into the provided Excel datasheet (Supplementary File) and retain the final values for reporting.
